requirements.requirement: Every sudo command run on node1 is recorded to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and a timestamp
requirements.summary: A sudoers snippet at /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging (Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log") was installed with 0440 root:root perms after visudo -cf validation. Subsequent sudo invocations by root and by a temporary test user 'sudologtest' were both correctly appended to the file with timestamp, user, PWD, and COMMAND fields (cmd-ee028bf5602b483f, cmd-349555fc00a242bd). Post-reboot, a fresh sudo command was again correctly logged (cmd-8315fdf08f9f4c91), confirming durability across restart.

requirements.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log (secure/messages/journal)
requirements.summary: Baseline evidence (cmd-f4211485b7854350) showed sudo COMMAND= lines appearing in /var/log/secure and journalctl before the change. After adding 'Defaults !syslog' to the sudoers snippet, /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and journalctl -t sudo were re-checked for both a root sudo call and a sudologtest sudo call, and no COMMAND= lines appeared in any of them (cmd-37eeff8e7f7e4c6c, cmd-1127e2552d77446c). Post-reboot re-verification (cmd-8315fdf08f9f4c91) confirmed /var/log/secure still shows no COMMAND lines for a new sudo invocation.

requirements.requirement: Configuration is correctly and safely installed (valid syntax, proper file placement/permissions)
requirements.summary: The sudoers addition was syntax-checked with visudo -cf before installation (cmd-6f29b492e28d49b9, cmd-4491ab570bc84978), then placed at /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging with 0440 root:root permissions, and the log file was pre-created with 0600 root:root permissions (cmd-3fa4ac57bd9c40fb).

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol, not part of the public task) node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered configuration/logging behavior
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64 along with the sudoers config and log contents (cmd-2dd584353a30499d), matching the fixed before_prepare boot-identity observation. 'systemctl reboot' was triggered and acknowledged before the connection dropped (cmd-43bbf73a5a9c4f71), the node was briefly unreachable (cmd-b12e74141358434e), then came back with a different boot_id 316d203c-8b2b-4777-97e6-b48341fd9a35 (cmd-179482e8887d41bd), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity observation. Post-restart, the sudoers config, log file content, and correct logging/exclusion behavior were all re-verified as intact (cmd-8315fdf08f9f4c91), demonstrating a full healthy-baseline -> disruption -> restoration -> recovered-state cycle.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct, corroborating evidence: sudo commands on node1 are now logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and these entries are verifiably excluded from /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and the journal, both before and after a real reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed well, with a clear pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged restart, a changed boot identity, and confirmed recovery of both the configuration and its logging behavior. The main blemish is minor leftover temp files (/tmp/sudo-logging, /tmp/x) that were not cleaned up, though they pose no functional or security risk.
limitations: Evidence is drawn from bounded stdout excerpts of a single verification pass; long-term durability of the syslog exclusion beyond the observed window (e.g., under sudo plugin updates) was not tested.

Cleanup of the temporary 'sudologtest' user required a retry (initial userdel failed due to an active session) before succeeding; the final state confirms removal, but the intermediate failure shows the first cleanup attempt was incomplete.
Two small residual files (/tmp/sudo-logging, /tmp/x) remain per the after-executor snapshot; their exact provenance/content of /tmp/x could not be fully confirmed from the redacted command text.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were largely well-scoped: a draft /tmp/sudo-logging file (cmd-6f29b492e28d49b9) was superseded by a corrected version (cmd-4491ab570bc84978) before install; a temporary test user 'sudologtest' and its sudoers entry, created for verification (cmd-97672c619f2e4683), were fully removed by the end (cleanup began in cmd-1127e2552d77446c and completed in cmd-f65c04aba6684f13 after an initial failed userdel due to an active session). One discovery attempt to test as 'cloud-user' failed harmlessly with no state change (cmd-90511507071343ec). However, the after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows residual files not cleaned up: /tmp/sudo-logging (the draft/staging sudoers file used before final install) and /tmp/x (a leftover redirect target from the test-user verification command in cmd-97672c619f2e4683) both remain on disk with no evidence of removal. /tmp/reboot.log is an expected, low-risk artifact of the backgrounded reboot trigger. These leftover temp files are minor, non-sensitive, and low-risk, but represent unnecessary residue that was not restored to the pre-task state.
